messages:
Sam: :rotating_light: incident-bot paging: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/streaming in us-west-2 - SLO breach. Automatic alert thresholds hit (p95 420ms -> 800ms, p99 1.6s -> 4.8s). Root ts 4412345678
IncidentBot: Automatic classification: multi-tenant GPU pool IO contention suspected (shared-nvme-3). Creating thread and paging oncall.
Tara: I'm on it. Pinged oncall.
Mike: joining. seeing tail latency and a bunch of streaming stalls in prod-rt streaming worker logs.
Dina: sending current dashboard link: https://dash.internal/redwood/streams/us-west-2?range=15m
Leo: confirmed >40% of streaming sessions saw partial frames drop >300ms for last 12m. Throughput hasn't dropped — looks like stalls not outage.
Sam: customer impact: a few enterprise customers reported slow chat responses (tickets #6543, #6546). Not yet escalated externally.
Priya: can we identify which tenants are high IO? run qdisc and iostat on the host with highest tail.
Mike: running: ssh gpu-host-24 "sudo iostat -dx 1 5" -> spikes on nvme1n1 with util 98%, avg await high
Mike: also `nvidia-smi dmon` shows some kernels with abnormal memcpy durations.
Tara: looks like noisy neighbor. Which cgroup does that container belong to? query: `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/machine.slice/*/cgroup.procs | xargs -I{} grep -H "container-" /proc/{}/cmdline`
Dina: attaching excerpt of streaming worker logs:
```
[2026-07-15T18:12:09Z] stream-session-id=73ab processing chunk size=512 tokens
[2026-07-15T18:12:11Z] stall detected: waiting for nvme read (timeout 2000ms)
[2026-07-15T18:12:12Z] retrying kv-cache fetch
[2026-07-15T18:12:13Z] session-circuit-breaker: tail-latency > 2000ms
```
Leo: host-level dmesg shows repeated blk_mq timeout and writeback bursts.
Sam: immediate mitigation options: 1) evict suspected tenant pods from shared-nvme-3 to alternate pool, 2) increase per-cgroup IO weight for streaming-critical class, 3) enable local KV cache bypass to reduce NVMe reads for streaming flows. Thoughts?
Priya: short-term safest is to evict heavy IO tenant to avoid collateral. Who owns the heavy tenant? run `rctl tenant-io --top 10`
Mike: `rctl` output: tenant-ids: t-889 (40% IO), t-205 (18%), t-301 (5%). t-889 is likely culprit.
Tara: t-889 corresponds to acme-data (enterprise). Should we notify support/AE before evicting?
Sam: Notify support but prioritize SLOs. We'll evict with immediate migration to dedicated-temp pool (burst nodes) and message support.
Dina: kicking off evacuation job: `kubectl label pod -l tenant=t-889 migrate=urgent && ./placement/migrate --from shared-nvme-3 --to burst-gpu-pool --tenant t-889`
IncidentBot: Evac job started by Dina at 4412345725
Priya: monitoring IO after migration...
Mike: migration started, initial pods terminating, new pods creating on burst-gpu-pool.
Leo: NVMe util dropping from 98% -> 45% within 60s on gpu-host-24
Dina: streaming p99 improved from 4.8s -> 900ms in the first 2m after migration.
Tara: good. Keep watching for any regressions or other noisy tenants.
Sam: we should apply a medium-term change: tighten io.weight for streaming-cgroup from 100 to 400 on shared pool, and set writeback limits. Priya can implement a safe cgroup change with a gradual ramp.
Priya: will create a runbook step: `echo 400 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/streaming-cg/blkio.weight` but will ramp in increments of 50 every 30s to avoid starve.
Mike: verifying KV-cache hit rates - cache misses dropped after migration by ~28% -> fewer backend reads.
Leo: customer tickets #6543/#6546 updated: latency explanation + mitigation note. Support notified.
Dina: starting post-incident sampling: capture `strace` on a sample streaming worker to confirm whether syscall wait is NVMe read or network. `sudo strace -p $pid -e trace=read,write,open,close -s 200 -o /tmp/strace-$pid.log`
Sam: handoff: oncall shift change in 20m. Tara will own live mitigation followed by handoff to Eng-SRE for root cause and perf tuning. Assigning follow-ups:
- Mike: confirm t-889 IO pattern and file a noisy-tenant ticket
- Priya: implement gradual cgroup blkio weight ramp and document runbook
- Leo: coordinate with infra to consider making burst-gpu-pool default for heavy IO tenants
- Dina: collect traces/log samples & attach to incident ticket
- Sam: update incident timeline and customer comms draft
Tara: acknowledged, will take live
IncidentBot: PagerDuty note: escalation suppressed, oncall acknowledged by Tara at 4412345782
Priya: applied first ramp: weight 150 -> seeing no undue starvation. Monitoring for 5m.
Mike: adding perf counter dump from host 24: `perf stat -e cycles,instructions,cache-misses -p $pid -- sleep 1` -> high cache-miss rate during stall windows.
Leo: likely combination: high IO queue + cache thrash + memcpy pauses. Root cause probably tenant-level sequential writes blocking NVMe queue.
Dina: collecting heap/profiler for model-serving process for later analysis.
Sam: current status: mitigation successful, p95 ~ 350ms, p99 ~ 820ms (still above target but trending down). Eviction of t-889 reduced contention. We'll keep incident open for RCA and follow-up remediation.
Tara: will stay monitoring during handoff. If any regression, page the secondary oncall.
SupportBot: created ticket INC-2026-332 with customer impact summary and mitigation timeline.
Sam: postmortem owners: Mike (RCA), Priya (mitigations/runbook), Leo (capacity & placement policy), Dina (observability additions). Target initial RCA draft in 48h.
Priya: will also propose an automated detection: flag tenants with >30% sustained nvme util for 3m and auto-migrate to burst pool.
Mike: note for post-incident: consider adding async read pipelining and prefetch heuristics to reduce blocking nvme reads during streaming.
Sam: thanks all. closing live mitigation loop. Final note: no data loss reported, customer latency incidents limited to a small subset and support notified. Will convert thread to incident channel summary after RCA draft.
Tara: copying timeline into incident doc now.
Leo: thumbs up :thumbsup:
LastAction: incident marked stable at 4412345898, monitoring continues.
